notes: Definition idealLevel restored to its pinned meaning. On v4.36, `multiplicity a b` is `(emultiplicity a b).toNat`, which is 0 when the multiplicity is infinite; the pinned value was `(emultiplicity a b).untopD 1`, which is 1. idealLevel takes an arbitrary ideal 𝔪, including ⊥ where the multiplicity is infinite, so its body is now written `(emultiplicity v.asIdeal 𝔪).untopD 1`, the pinned definition unfolded and identical on every input. idealLevel_le_ker_iff (which assumes 𝔪 ≠ ⊥) rewrites this back to `multiplicity` with FiniteMultiplicity.of_prime_left before the unchanged rw chain. finprod_asIdeal_pow_dvd_iff still states `multiplicity v.asIdeal I`, but it assumes `I ≠ ⊥` and v.asIdeal is prime, so the multiplicity is finite and the old and new values agree; it is left unchanged. The reused-names audit reports only that theorem afterwards.
